item.title: John Carmack on the mistakes around Quake that ruined id software
item.description:
📝 Quake was overly ambitious technically. One real problem that I don’t accept the blame for is that we were insisting that level designers be not just game designers, but also have strong visual design esthetics. Romero covered that well, which set our company expectations early on.
🔗 Read more: https://twitter.com/ID_AA_Carmack/status/2069799283369345247

item.title: CAPTCHAs have failed for 20 years
item.description:
📝 TL;DR: Every CAPTCHA generation (distorted text, harder text, image grids) was eventually beaten by machines. The same advances that digitized books and read street signs made computers capable CAPTCHA solvers. Then machine learning arrived.
🔗 Read more: https://www.browserbase.com/blog/why-captchas-are-getting-harder

item.description:

item.title: For Most of the World, Open-Source AI Is the Only Way Forward
item.description:

He extends the analogy to mobile networks, noting that “your cell phone regularly actually runs an open-source operating system… and it talks to a cell phone tower that runs an open-source software stack.

item.title: Running Windows Games on a Hobby OS with Wine
item.description:
📝 While Astral did have OpenGL, Wine explicitly needs EGL to work, which Astral's Mesa port did not provide. This was accomplished using Wine's WoW64 mode, which does not need any 32-bit Unix libraries. With this fixed, scoresheet upload works.
🔗 Read more: https://astral-os.org/posts/2026/04/03/wine-on-astral.html
